unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 9-LEVEL: B1.1 THEME 8: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE & FUTURE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: They write and design the content of a futuristic film script and then they present and apply it as a film-showing event in class by inviting other students as actors, actresses, directors etc. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: It is generally accepted that people who start to learn a new language bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning. For instance, this theme is based on the concept of ''films, film genres, futuristic films with futuristic ideas, and technology'' and it is present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. People who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. For instance, a student of an upper-secondary school in year 9, may know what a film is, what film genres are, what kind of films the futuristic films could be, but will not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However, students could be able to recognise and express such situations in their own language, and this knowledge would prepare them to recognise the same concepts later in their foreign language, English. In terms of preparation for the current new theme, it is assumed that they have learnt some basic words about films or other entertaining content such as ''an actor, a film, a comedy, a drama, a romance.'' and how to describe their feelings about them with adjectives such as ''exciting, funny, scary, good, real, interesting, etc.'' and how to talk about them by using some structures such as ''What’s/is it/this? It’s/is a film. What kind of a film is it? It’s/is a comedy film. What kind of films do you like? I like comedies. Do you like dramas? No, I don’t.'' in English from the previous themes or years. These grammar items and vocabulary can be used as a basis for learning the new language grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is expected that the physical, cognitive, affective, and social factors are appropriate and suitable for students to learn about ''films, film genres, futuristic films with futuristic ideas, and technology''. Therefore, a contextual close (gapped) test about ''films'' could be given to the students for remembering and practising the previously learnt items could be delivered to discuss and fill in the blanks with the required words and phrases in pairs. This session can help them revise all the vocabulary and grammatical items used from previous themes or previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how much they use these items correctly to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise or practise in order to revise previous knowledge and to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about futuristic films in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Futuristic Film Promotion In this activity, students work in small groups and brainstorm a futuristic film idea, including the genre (e.g., time travel), plot (e.g., robots saving or harming humanity), and characters (e.g., an adventurous crew). Each group collaborates to develop and present their film promotion to the class. They use descriptive adjectives such as futuristic, advanced, technological to enhance their presentation. As a final product, students design a poster that displays their film idea, featuring its title, key elements, and visuals to represent their concept. After each presentation, the teacher and peers give constructive feedback, focusing on creativity, use of target vocabulary, and clarity of ideas. They also provide positive reinforcement feedback to help students refine their language and teamwork skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students reconstruct a futuristic film concept in English through an interactive information gap activity by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Reconstructing the Film Schema In this activity, students work in groups and are provided with different parts of a text describing a futuristic film (e.g., the plot, characters, and futuristic elements such as space exploration or advanced technology). Each group member receives a unique section of the text to read individually. One student from the group stands at the board to create a film schema, including elements like the title, main plot, characters, and key futuristic themes. Group members, after reading their parts, explain the information to the student at the board in their own words, ensuring they use the target vocabulary such as futuristic, advanced, technological and the target grammar where appropriate (e.g., ''The film will focus on robots saving humanity''.2). The student at the board uses the shared information to fill in the schema. In the end, the teacher reveals the original film schema, and the class compares it to the reconstructed version. The groups discuss the differences and provide feedback on the accuracy and clarity of their communication. The teacher and peers give constructive feedback, highlighting effective explanations, use of vocabulary, and teamwork, while offering suggestions for improvement. This activity ensures active participation and collaborative learning while fostering critical thinking and language development. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To help students describe different film genres in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Film Genre Match-Up In this activity, students receive a worksheet containing film genre names such as comedy, action, time travel, and space adventure alongside images representing each genre. They match each image with the correct genre name, helping them associate vocabulary with visual cues. To reinforce support and enhance their understanding, students write one sentence about their favourite genre by using target language items, for example, ''Comedy films make people laugh''. A word bank with genre names and sample sentences is provided to guide them. At the end of the activity, students actively share their sentences with the class or in small groups, fostering engagement and allowing them to practice the target vocabulary. After sharing, the teacher and peers provide feedback, focusing on sentence accuracy, use of target vocabulary, and creativity. Positive reinforcement is used to encourage participation and highlight successful language use, helping students to build confidence and improve their skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective : To talk about futuristic ideas in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Futuristic Sentence Builder In this activity, students are provided with sentence fragments on physical cards (e.g., ''Robots will'', ''help people'', ''in the future'') or digital cards using web 2.0 tools if available. Students rearrange the fragments to create meaningful and grammatically correct sentences, focusing on futuristic ideas. For those without access to web 2.0 tools, teachers can distribute printed sentence fragments or write them on the board for group work. Visual aids such as printed or drawn pictures of robots, space exploration, and alien invasions can be used to stimulate ideas. After students create their sentences, they read them aloud to the class or in small groups. The teacher and peers provide constructive feedback, focusing on accuracy, creativity, and use of target vocabulary. Positive reinforcement is encouraged to build confidence and highlight successful usage of the target language. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
